title: Vacuum Toilet Bowl Interface and Odour Seal Improvement

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Replaces the bowl to shroud interface seal and the toilet assembly latching arrangement, following persistent odour complaints traced to a seal that relaxes after repeated servicing rather than to the waste system itself.

sections.reason: Odour complaints in the mid and aft lavatories were the single largest cabin dissatisfaction item reported by three operators, running at roughly four complaints per thousand passengers on long sectors. Teardown of twelve returned assemblies showed the bowl to shroud seal taking a permanent set after about eighteen months of servicing cycles, leaving a gap of up to one and a half millimetres at the aft edge that the flush cycle draws air through in the wrong direction.
sections.description: The interface seal is replaced by a two lip design in a different compound, retained by a revised partition bracket that carries the seal groove rather than clamping the seal against the shroud. The latch assembly, which had to be over-centred to compress the old seal, is replaced by a lower force variant, and the servicing panel cable tie standard is changed so the harness behind the shroud is no longer pulled against the new bracket. The waste tank, the drain line and the flush control are unchanged; this modification stops at the bowl interface.
sections.effects: Mass increase of zero point six kilograms per lavatory, distributed through the cabin. No electrical load change. Interchangeable at aircraft level; the latch and the seal must be changed as a set. The servicing task changes because the latch closing force and the seal seating check are new, and the parts catalogue figure gains a pre and post modification item pair. No dispatch effect.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in at MSN M00272. Retrofit is by bulletin at any A check, roughly three hours per lavatory, with the kit covering all lavatories on one aircraft.

type_data.production_impact: Cut in at MSN M00272, supplied as a lavatory monument kit
